name: Osaka Itami International Airport
before:
The closest airport to Osaka, 11 km north of Osaka Station, and closer to Kyoto than anything else at 36 km. It is the primary domestic airport for the whole Kansai region.

The name is the trap. Until January 2025 this was called Osaka International Airport, and that is still its official Japanese name, but it handles domestic flights only. Every international service moved to Kansai International, 43 km away, in 1994. A client booked to Osaka may be arriving at either, so check the code.

There is a single terminal with 21 gates, split into a North Terminal for JAL and Amakusa Airlines and a South Terminal for ANA and IBEX, joined by a Central Block of shops, restaurants and a hotel. A renovation begun in 2016 delivered a consolidated central area in 2018.

It carried 16.3 million passengers in 2018, seventh busiest in Japan, on a site of only 311 hectares.

The airport takes its name from Itami in Hyōgo Prefecture, where most of its land sits, though it also spreads into Toyonaka and Ikeda.
after:
Kansai's main domestic airport, 11 km north of central Osaka and about 55 minutes by bus from Kyoto Station.

The name is the trap. Its official Japanese name is still Osaka International Airport, though it now calls itself Osaka Itami Airport in English, and it handles domestic flights only. International flights moved to Kansai International when that airport opened in 1994. A client booked to Osaka may be arriving at either, so check the code.

The terminal is split into a North Terminal for JAL and Amakusa Airlines and a South Terminal for ANA and IBEX. A renovation opened a new central area in 2018 and was completed in August 2020.

Japan's transport ministry counted just over 16 million passengers here in 2025, on a site of only 311 hectares.

claims.claim: Kansai's main domestic airport
claims.note: Was 'the primary domestic airport for the whole Kansai region', moved to the opening. The Osaka Civil Aviation Bureau's preliminary table for calendar 2025 has Itami at 16,175,135 domestic passengers against 6,571,221 at Kansai and 3,654,633 at Kobe. The table prints the airport names apart from the figures, so the rows were tied to names by the regional total: the Kinki rows (Itami 16,175,135, Kansai 34,034,435, Yao 0, Nanki-Shirahama 247,436, Kobe 4,059,871 and Tajima 39,946) add up exactly to the Kinki total of 54,556,823, and the 16.2 million row has no international passengers in any month, which of the region's large airports fits only Itami (Kansai and Kobe both carry international passengers).

claims.claim: the transport ministry counted just over 16 million passengers in 2025
claims.inAfter: Japan's transport ministry counted just over 16 million passengers here in 2025
claims.note: Was '16.3 million passengers in 2018'. MLIT's Osaka Civil Aviation Bureau counts 16,175,135 passengers for calendar 2025 (preliminary) and 16,286,822 for the year to March 2026, all domestic. Attributed, because no second count could be read: the operator's monthly traffic reports sit on its corporate site, which answers plain requests with 403 and refuses both link listers, so no report address could be found (the one Wikipedia cites is for December 2024), and the owner NKIAC's results for the year to March 2026 give no traffic. The operator's own profile page says about 17 million a year, undated, which is not used. Wikipedia's infobox gives 15,157,501 for 2024.

claims.why: The North and South Terminals are kept (see above). The 21 gates rest on Wikipedia alone: the operator's terminal map at the address Wikipedia cites returns 404, and its passenger site draws its maps and access details in script, so they could not be read.

claims.claim: a Central Block of shops, restaurants and a hotel
claims.wasBefore: joined by a Central Block of shops, restaurants and a hotel
claims.why: The operator confirms a central area (opened 2018, kept above) and a hotel (its timeline: 大阪空港ホテル renovated in December 2017), but not where the hotel sits or what the central area holds; that rests on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: a renovation begun in 2016 delivered a consolidated central area in 2018
claims.wasBefore: A renovation begun in 2016 delivered a consolidated central area in 2018.
claims.why: The start is disputed: the operator's timeline dates the start of works (着工) to April 2015 and a safety ceremony for them to February 2016, while Wikipedia says work began in February 2016. 'Consolidated' rests on Wikipedia alone. Replaced by the 2018 central area and the August 2020 completion (see above).

claims.claim: 16.3 million passengers in 2018
claims.why: Eight years old. Replaced by the transport ministry's 2025 count (see above).

claims.claim: seventh busiest in Japan
claims.why: A 2018 ranking the operator does not state. MLIT's national ranking tables are Excel files the sweep's tools cannot save, so no current rank could be confirmed.

claims.claim: named after Itami, where most of its land is, spreading into Toyonaka and Ikeda
claims.wasBefore: The airport takes its name from Itami in Hyōgo Prefecture, where most of its land sits, though it also spreads into Toyonaka and Ikeda.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. Itami City's airport page that Wikipedia cites is gone (404) and its airport section could not be found; the Osaka Civil Aviation Bureau's pages give no location. The operator's head office address, 大阪府豊中市蛍池西町 (Toyonaka, Osaka), bears out Toyonaka only. Worth restoring if the city's page turns up.

claims.claim: Kobe Airport now has international flights too
claims.why: Held back: verified but replaces nothing in the old text. The operator now lists Kobe Airport as international and domestic, and the transport ministry's 2025 table shows Kobe's first international passengers in April 2025 (405,238 in the year). So a client booked to the Osaka area could also land at Kobe.

opinion.why: Framing carried over from the old text. The official Japanese name (Osaka International Airport) and the English name the operator now uses (Osaka Itami Airport) differ, and the airport has no international flights, which is the confusion Wikipedia says the English renaming was meant to end.

opinion.text: A client booked to Osaka may be arriving at either, so check the code.
opinion.why: Advice carried over from the old text. Kansai International has domestic flights as well as international ones (the operator lists it as international and domestic; the transport ministry counts 6,571,221 domestic passengers there in 2025).
